SMTO-GWT-0060 — SMTO can't find that GPU on the Gateway

GUID: b13ceffb-1f4f-5c96-970c-b6dbfe5f8368
Slug: gpu-device-not-found
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gpu

What happened

  • The GPU you asked about isn't in the list of GPUs the Gateway computer can see right now. It may have been removed, renumbered or be on another Gateway. SMTO didn't change any GPU settings.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to list the GPUs on this Gateway. GPU numbers can change after a restart, so the current list shows which GPUs are really there.
  2. Make sure you are working on the right Gateway. Check the Gateway selected for this conversation. The GPU may be in a different computer than the one this request went to.
  3. Ask for the action again, naming the GPU by its ID (UUID) from the new list. The ID stays the same even when GPU numbers change.
  4. If a GPU you expect is missing from the list, run nvidia-smi on the Gateway computer and restart that computer if the GPU is missing there too. A GPU that the computer itself can't see won't appear in SMTO either.

What success looks like

  • The GPU appears in the list, and your request for it completes without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer, noting which GPU you expected to see.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The requested GPU index or UUID is not in the Gateway's current NVIDIA device list, or nvidia-smi reported device-not-found.

What this means

  • Current GPU discovery could not find the requested device, or the NVIDIA provider returned its device-not-found exit classification. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Current GPU discovery could not find the requested device, or the NVIDIA provider returned its device-not-found exit classification.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the requested UUID or index with gpu.devices on the original Gateway; do not substitute another device by index.

How to fix it

  • Run gpu.devices on the intended Gateway to list current UUIDs and indexes, then resubmit using the exact UUID from that list. If the device should exist, check nvidia-smi -L on the host for a GPU that has dropped off the bus or a changed device order.
  • Discover current UUIDs with gpu.devices.

Retry and execution caution

  • Discover current UUIDs with gpu.devices.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended UUID is present and resolves consistently before further device work.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, kill GPU clients automatically or invent sensor values.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
